def: Model Context Protocol: a standard for exposing tools, resources, and prompts from an external system to an AI application.

term: MCP connector vs full MCP client
def: The connector calls a remote MCP server from the API surface; a full client manages transport, session, and tool lifecycle itself. Choosing one is a trust-boundary and operations decision, not a convenience one.
A tool your application executes after Claude emits tool_use; you own authorization, validation, and the returned tool_result.
A tool executed on Anthropic's side within the request; you configure and constrain it but do not run the code.
The structured request/response pair that carries an agentic turn: tool_use is model output naming a tool and arguments; tool_result is the application's answer.
A caller-supplied identifier that makes a repeated write produce one effect, which is what makes retries and duplicate deliveries safe.
Deliberately slowing or queueing work in response to 429s and capacity signals instead of retrying immediately.
Asynchronous bulk processing for work no interactive user is waiting on, traded against latency for cost and throughput.
Schema-enforced response shape for machine consumers, stronger than asking the model to 'always return valid JSON'.
The extent of damage a failure or compromise in one component can reach; bounded by scoping credentials, tools, tenancy, and isolation.
Model reasons, requests a tool, observes the result, and continues until a stop condition. Bounds on turns, spend, and time are part of the design.
Delegated agent with isolated context returning a result to a parent; the primary win is context isolation, parallelism second.
Retrieval-augmented generation: fetch relevant evidence at request time rather than carrying the whole corpus in context.
Long context suits a bounded, mostly-relevant corpus; retrieval suits a large or fast-changing one needing citations and scale.
A second-stage scorer that reorders retrieved candidates by relevance before they enter context.
The system that owns authoritative state. A transcript, a model's reasoning, and a project instruction file are never it.
A required approval before a consequential or irreversible action; the threshold is set by risk and policy, not model confidence alone.
A pattern where a coordinating agent decomposes work to specialized workers, keeping each worker's context and authority narrow.
A representative, versioned test set plus a scoring method, defined before prompt tuning begins.
A curated set of cases with known-correct outcomes used as a regression anchor across model and prompt changes.
Using a model to score outputs against a rubric; useful at scale, and itself something that needs calibration against human labels.
Attributing a bad answer to the specific layer that caused it: retrieval, prompt, model, tool, application logic, or source data.
An automated check that blocks a change when measured quality, cost, or latency falls below an agreed threshold.
The committed service level (for example p95 latency or success rate) that a scenario's design and escalation paths must hold.
A timed, attributed unit of work in a distributed trace, letting you separate retrieval, model, and tool time in one request.
Untrusted content attempting to act as instruction. The defense is architectural: treat retrieved and user content as data, and keep authority in code.
The line where untrusted input enters, where deterministic control ends and model reasoning begins, and where a human must approve.
Default-deny inspection before model ingress and tool egress so sensitive data does not cross a boundary unexamined.
Separating identity, storage, retrieval scope, keys, and authorization per tenant so one customer's context cannot reach another's.
Immutable record of decisions, control outcomes, model identity, and approvals — metadata sufficient to reconstruct, without storing prompt bodies.
Zero Data Retention: a contractual and product-dependent arrangement under which inputs and outputs are not retained. Eligibility is not universal.
Holding credentials in a managed store with short-lived workload identity, never in prompts, client code, or repository files.
When authorization, data, or a dependency is uncertain, stop or escalate rather than produce a confident action.
Unit economics denominated in the business result a human accepts, not in tokens or requests — the figure a stakeholder can act on.
A cumulative evidence requirement a change must satisfy at each stage from development through production.
The hash tying every stage's evidence to one build; a rebuild between stages invalidates the earlier evidence.
Files changed, tests, evals, residual risks, and rollback — the handoff artifact that makes a change reviewable.
Recovery time and recovery point objectives: how fast service must return and how much data loss is tolerable.
The pre-agreed way to revert a change, including data and prompt/model version, without depending on the change's author.
Architecture decision record: the durable statement of a decision, its alternatives, and its consequences.
Passing every gate means a change may be reviewed for deployment; a human still authorizes it.
The unit of model processing and billing; context and cost are counted in tokens, not pages.
The working set for one request: system instructions, history, tool definitions, retrieved documents, and tool results all consume it.
The cap on generated output for a request. It is not the context window, and hitting it surfaces as a max_tokens stop_reason.
Why generation stopped — end_turn, tool_use, max_tokens, and others — and therefore what the application should do next.
Reusing a stable processed prefix to cut repeated cost and latency; it rewards putting durable content first and volatile content last.
Summarizing or pruning earlier turns so a long session stays within budget without losing the facts the task depends on.
Sending routine work to the cheapest model that meets quality and escalating ambiguous or high-stakes cases deliberately.
Configurable additional reasoning before the answer, traded against latency and cost, and summarized rather than exposed verbatim.
Project context and conventions for Claude Code. It is guidance, not a security control.
On-demand packaged procedure or knowledge, loaded when relevant instead of bloating every turn's context.
A lifecycle-event handler that runs deterministically — the right home for a must-never-happen rule that prose cannot enforce.
What an agent may invoke, and isolated filesystem and git state when several agents work at once; both are blast-radius controls.
The library surface for building custom agents with the same loop, tool, and permission primitives Claude Code uses.
